headline: Dry Beppu tour; rain possible late, In-fa far from cruise route
summary: Beppu's geothermal and monkey-park tour should remain dry. Showers are more likely after sightseeing, while Typhoon In-fa remains far southeast of the Seven Seas Explorer's remaining route. No verified Regent schedule change.

weather.summary: 23°C / 10°C (73°F / 50°F) · Sunny to partly cloudy, rain risk later
details: October 29 forecast: 0–10% chance of rain through the daytime sightseeing period, rising to about 50% from 6 PM to midnight; late-evening rain timing remains uncertain.
During the 11 AM–2 PM Beppu Hells and monkey-park tour, meaningful rain is not expected. Carry a light layer for the cooler morning and a compact umbrella for the evening.
Local forecast reflects Beppu/Oita rather than precise conditions aboard the ship.

typhoon.status: No significant typhoon threat to upcoming ports
typhoon.summary: JMA's 29 October 06:45 JST advisory places very strong Typhoon In-fa far southeast of mainland Japan. The current forecast keeps its center near the Mariana/Ogasawara Islands through 31 October, far south of the Beppu–Tokyo route. Champi transitioned to an extratropical low on October 25.
details: 29 October 06:00 JST observation: 15.8°N, 155.5°E, near Minamitorishima; 945 hPa; sustained winds 45 m/s (162 km/h), gusts 65 m/s (234 km/h); moving west at 25 km/h.

Since 28 October 06:00 JST: position shifted west and slightly north; central pressure decreased 950→945 hPa while peak sustained winds decreased 50→45 m/s. The 30 October forecast predicts renewed intensification to 935 hPa.
JMA projects In-fa near 17.1°N, 149.0°E by 30 October 06:00 and 19.8°N, 144.0°E by 31 October 03:00 JST, then near the Ogasawara Islands November 1. Track uncertainty grows beyond 48 hours.

Seven Seas Explorer: low direct tropical-storm risk for Beppu today, October 30 at sea, and Tokyo October 31. Distant swell is possible but cannot be quantified without the actual sailing route and marine forecasts.
No Regent-confirmed port cancellations, route changes, or shore-excursion changes were verified. Ship announcements take precedence.
